brief.keyMessage: When school stops, free school meals stop too. Your gift keeps a family fed through half term, and right now it goes twice as far.

creativeContext.problemInDailyLife: Parents skip meals so their children can eat, and say nothing.
creativeContext.storySeed: My neighbour skipped dinner most nights so her kids could eat, and never told anyone.
creativeContext.openingQuestion: Do you know which family on your street skipped dinner last night?
creativeContext.whatWeDo: runs community kitchens and school breakfast clubs so no child starts the day hungry.
creativeContext.caseStudy: Last February a dad of three in Oldham was working nights and still running out of food by Wednesday. Kindred Kitchens' community fridge and a weekly parcel got the family through half term, and the breakfast club meant the kids ate before school every day. Names and details changed to protect privacy; the case is real.

references: Previous appeal: UGC from a volunteer packing parcels outperformed studio video on ROAS

ranked.title: Two kitchen tables, one difference
ranked.hook: Same street. Same week. One kitchen table has what it needs. One doesn't.
ranked.concept: A split-frame creative showing two near-identical kitchen tables: one with what it needs, one without. The only difference is a £20 gift. Copy explains that £20 fills a family food parcel for a week.
ranked.whyItWorks: Contrast makes an invisible problem visible in under two seconds, and the £20 price tag answers "what does my money actually do".
ranked.audienceInsight: Cannot stand the thought of a child going without
ranked.visualDirection: Split screen of two kitchen tables, warm vs cold colour grade, one line of copy across the seam, logo bottom right.

ranked.title: Do you know which family on your street skipped dinner last night
ranked.hook: Do you know which family on your street skipped dinner last night?
ranked.concept: Opens with a question the audience is already half-asking, then widens it to ending child food poverty in the uk and the £90 ask.
ranked.whyItWorks: A personal question earns the first second of attention without shock imagery.
ranked.audienceInsight: Wants to know a gift is used well
ranked.visualDirection: Presenter to camera for UGC; for static, the question in large type over a kitchen table scene.

ranked.title: The number behind the ask
ranked.hook: £90. That is what it takes: funds a week of fresh fruit and veg for a community fridge.
ranked.concept: A single oversized number fills the frame with a short line underneath: "funds a week of fresh fruit and veg for a community fridge". Supporting line cites: £45 stocks a school breakfast club for a week.
ranked.whyItWorks: A specific, small number removes the 'drop in the ocean' feeling and makes the ask feel finishable.
ranked.audienceInsight: Wants to know a gift is used well
ranked.visualDirection: Flat brand background, huge numeral in accent colour, a tight crop of the kitchen table in the lower third.

ranked.title: Myth: food banks are only for people out of work
ranked.hook: "food banks are only for people out of work." Here is what actually happens.
ranked.concept: Directly tackles the objection "Thinks food banks are only for people out of work" in the first line, then explains the gap Kindred Kitchens fills and what £20 does about it.
ranked.whyItWorks: Naming the objection first earns trust and pre-empts the scroll-past.
ranked.audienceInsight: Thinks food banks are only for people out of work
ranked.visualDirection: Text-first creative: objection struck through, answer beneath, presenter to camera for video.

ranked.title: Ride along with the Kindred Kitchens team
ranked.hook: We filmed one Tuesday with the Kindred Kitchens team. This is what £45 looks like in real life.
ranked.concept: Documentary-style footage of the team doing the work the donation funds (stocks a school breakfast club for a week). No actors, no music swells, just the work.
ranked.whyItWorks: Showing the operation answers the admin-cost worry better than any pie chart.
ranked.audienceInsight: Worried the money goes on admin
ranked.visualDirection: Handheld, natural sound, captions throughout, team in branded jackets, end card with the tier.

ranked.title: Thirty seconds from our director
ranked.hook: I run Kindred Kitchens. I want to tell you exactly where your £45 goes.
ranked.concept: A single unedited take of the charity director speaking plainly about the weeks ahead and the offer. No b-roll, captions only.
ranked.whyItWorks: Low production, high trust. Direct accountability answers the admin objection head on.
ranked.audienceInsight: Worried the money goes on admin
ranked.visualDirection: Phone camera, eye level, office or depot background, burned-in captions, 9:16.

ranked.title: From your gift to a family
ranked.hook: What happens in the first two days after you give £45?
ranked.concept: A three-step explainer: you give, we act, a family gets what they need. Each step shows the real person or system involved, ending with "stocks a school breakfast club for a week".
ranked.whyItWorks: Transparency about process is a direct response to the fear that money disappears into admin.
ranked.audienceInsight: Worried the money goes on admin
ranked.visualDirection: Three-panel carousel or 15s animation with simple icons in brand colours, one sentence per panel.

ranked.title: A letter you will not get
ranked.hook: Most people we help never write to thank anyone. This is the letter they would send.
ranked.concept: A handwritten-style letter from a family describing an ordinary good day, revealed line by line. Signed with a first name only. Closes with the £20 ask.
ranked.whyItWorks: The letter form slows the reader down and rewards attention with emotion rather than shock.
ranked.audienceInsight: Cannot stand the thought of a child going without
ranked.visualDirection: Paper texture, handwriting font animated as if being written, soft lamp light.
riskFlags: Must be clearly labelled as representative, not a real letter, unless consent exists

ranked.title: Doubled until the deadline
ranked.hook: Every gift matched by Fairfield Foods until 28 February.
ranked.concept: A countdown-led creative built around the match offer. £90 becomes £180 and the copy states exactly what that pays for twice over.
ranked.whyItWorks: Match funding is the strongest proven conversion lever in charity paid social; the deadline gives a reason to act today rather than someday.
ranked.audienceInsight: Wants to know a gift is used well
ranked.visualDirection: Bold accent background, the two amounts side by side with an arrow, deadline date in a sticker element.

ranked.title: Families in your postcode
ranked.hook: Within two miles of you: parents skip meals so their children can eat, and say nothing.
ranked.concept: Geo-personalised copy by region, with Kindred Kitchens's local track record (£45 stocks a school breakfast club for a week). The ask stays national; the framing feels like a neighbour.
ranked.whyItWorks: Proximity increases perceived responsibility and makes impact feel checkable.
ranked.audienceInsight: Wants to know a gift is used well
ranked.visualDirection: Map-pin style graphic over a local street at dusk, one kitchen table highlighted in accent colour.
riskFlags: Needs region-level ad set split for the personalised line
